name: GBL

tolerance.full: within several days of continuous use

addictionPotential: Highly physically and moderately to highly psychologically addictive
toxicities: FreeODwiki identifies GBL as a GHB prodrug and warns that combining GABAergic depressants with opioids, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, gabapentinoids, thienodiazepines or alcohol may cause fatal overdose. It specifically warns that stimulant comedown can leave a depressant effect overwhelming the user and causing respiratory arrest.
effectsSummary: The effect is extremely dose-dependent and varies greatly from individual to individual. It also depends on the purity of the substance. The spectrum of effects ranges from euphoria, relaxation, disinhibition, intensification of perception, urge to talk (babble flash), slight dizziness and drowsiness to deep (coma-like) sleep or unconsciousness.
dosageRemark: The archived oral table lists threshold 0.3 mL, light 0.3-0.9 mL, moderate 0.9-1.5 mL, strong 1.5-3 mL (the page warns >2 mL may induce deep sleep), heavy 3 mL+; total 1-2 h, onset 3-10 min, comeup 5-15 min, peak 30-45 min, offset 15-30 min and afterglow 1-3 h. Educational user/resource compilation, not a recommendation. GBL is converted in the body to GHB and 1 mL GBL is equivalent to 1.66 g sodium GHB; liquids of unknown concentration introduce uncertainty.
generalRisks: GBL is converted to GHB in the body. FreeODwiki warns strong sedation and potentially fatal overdose when combined with other depressants; it says doses above 2 mL may induce deep sleep and cautions that concentration of prepared liquids may be unknown.
longtermRisks: Regular use of GBL can lead to sleep disorders, anxiety and tremors; there is a risk of dependence with psychological and physical symptoms. In the case of chronic high-dose consumption (several doses daily), severe physical withdrawal symptoms such as sweating, muscle cramps or epileptic seizures occur upon discontinuation.
saferUse: FreeODwiki strongly advises against combining GBL/GHB with other depressants, especially at moderate to heavy doses, because of fatal overdose risk.
The archive warns prepared liquid concentration may be unknown; it distinguishes GBL volume from GHB mass and advises cross-checking its educational user/resource dose data.
summary: A pro-drug to GHB whose rapid absorption leads it to have a faster onset and shorter duration. Used in a similar manner to GHB, as a less-toxic alternative to alcohol. Consume slowly instead of as a "shot" to hugely improve safety and reduce overdose risk.
